transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Markus (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Novena), Kenji Sato (Novena SRE), Aisha Malik (Novena Data Science)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
- Reviewed lab bench results comparing Redwood runtime against incumbent (VeloxAI).

- Action items: quant runs, profiler logs, security sync, updated cost spreadsheet.

Topics:
1) Latency p50/p95 by sequence length
2) Throughput at target concurrency (200 QPS simulated)
3) Batch sizing and KV/prefix cache behavior
4) Quantization effect on quality and latency
5) Security/compliance checklist items (KMS, SSO, audit logs)

Transcript:
00:00 Sofia (Redwood AE): All right, thanks everyone for hopping on. want to try to run 45 minutes, we'll go through the bench numbers first then markus will walk through the profiler traces.
00:22 Priya (Novena): yep, thanks. we have kenji and aisha on as well. main goal today is to see if we can get p95 below our 350ms target on short prompts and understand throughput shape. also, where's the break-even vs Velox for cost.
00:48 Markus (Redwood SE): cool. quick note — some of the earlier runs used a slightly different kernel path, so i re-ran with the optimized attention patch (we call it fast-attn) but the log names might show "fast adtn" in the dump, just ignore that.
01:12 Kenji (Novena): fine. can you remind us which model variant you used for this run?
01:18 Markus (Redwood SE): sure — model-3, 8k context trimmed to 2k for the bench, running with q4_0 quant profile for most throughput tests; we also did fp16 baseline. the baseline vendor (VeloxAI) data was their public benchmark and our in-house replay against their docker image.
01:42 Aisha (Novena): okay, show us the headline numbers.
01:50 Sofia (Redwood AE): slide 2 — p50 for 32-token prompts is 42ms on Redwood, p95 is 210ms. Velox numbers for the same workload were p50 55ms, p95 290ms. so about ~25% p95 improvement in this slice.
02:20 Priya (Novena): that's promising. what about the 512-token sequences? our app will have some longer contexts.
02:31 Markus (Redwood SE): for 512 tokens, p50 420ms, p95 1.1s on our config but note we hit kv cache warm-up effects; the first few tokens are heavier. Velox reported p95 ~1.4s in public numbers, though their test used different batching.
03:05 Kenji (Novena): when you say kv cache, do you mean the K V cache — like prefix caching? are we able to preserve caches across requests in your setup?
03:16 Markus (Redwood SE): yes, prefix+KV cache works; in dedicated mode you can pin sessions to keep cache warm. in the hosted replay we simulated session affinity but there will be real-world misses.
03:34 Aisha (Novena): throughput numbers? our peak QPS simulated in pilot was 200 concurrent requests — what's throughput and p95 at that concurrency?
03:45 Markus (Redwood SE): at 200 QPS with batch size 8 we saw tokens/sec of ~9.6k and request throughput ~180 rps for short prompts, p95 drifted to ~260ms. at batch size 16 throughput improved but latency p95 crept up to ~420ms.
04:10 Priya (Novena): so there's a tradeoff between batching and latency, yeah. can you quantify cost per 1k tokens at those settings?
04:21 Sofia (Redwood AE): we'll send a cost breakdown. rough number from the pilot: at batch 8 q4_0 we estimate $0.80 per 1k tokens for production-like utilization; Velox reported $1.05 per 1k on their published sheet. we'll put exact math in the spreadsheet.
04:51 Kenji (Novena): transcript glitch — heard "q four zero" as "q for zero" in the logs earlier, just checking the quant scheme naming.
05:03 Markus (Redwood SE): right it's q4_0 in the repo; some exporter labels it q4zero so that's a naming mismatch.
05:20 Priya (Novena): any quality regressions with the q4 run? Aisha you looked at rouge/bleu-ish metrics?
05:30 Aisha (Novena): we did a small EM/semantic similarity run — delta was within noise on our eval set for the q4_0 config except for some rare hallucinations on long-context instructions.
05:48 Markus (Redwood SE): that's expected — quantization will occasionally nudge generation distributions. we can try q5_1 or mixed precision in the next run.
06:02 Sofia (Redwood AE): Markus, can you talk through the profiler traces — what were the hotspots?
06:12 Markus (Redwood SE): sure. i'll share the flamegraph link after. short version: kernel launch overhead dominated at low batch sizes (the cpu->gpu enqueue and small kernels), at larger batches matmul became dominant. we also saw some GPU memory copies around the KV scatter step — i suspect our memcpy path in that config is not fully fused. there's a note in the logs that the chosen kernel fallbacked to a generic GEMM for one layer — shows as "gemm-fallback" in traces.
07:04 Kenji (Novena): is that something you can patch quickly or is it model-specific?
07:12 Markus (Redwood SE): often it's a kernel-selector heuristic; we can tweak thresholds and recompile, might get another 5-8% latency improvement on those sequences.
07:30 Priya (Novena): what's the risk if we switch to dedicated pool vs hosted for the pilot? we care about isolation and cache pinning.
07:41 Sofia (Redwood AE): Dedicated gives you pinned GPU pools and session affinity which helps warm KV caches and consistent tail latencies. hosted is cheaper and faster to start but less control over cache warmness. for your SLAs, dedicated looks like the safer path.
08:05 Aisha (Novena): any implications for security — KMS, SSO?
08:11 Sofia (Redwood AE): dedicated and private both support customer-managed KMS and SAML SSO. we'll surface the SOC2 checklist in the security sync.
08:26 Priya (Novena): you mentioned fallback to a smaller model variant if capacity is constrained. do you have data how often fallback would trigger under our traffic pattern?
08:39 Markus (Redwood SE): with autoscaling and burst capacity we observed fallback only in extreme synthetic bursts above 2x expected peak. if you want conservative ops, we can reserve a burst buffer.
09:00 Kenji (Novena): got it. back to the bench — any regression tests vs the original pilot baseline (our in-house inference) besides Velox?
09:12 Sofia (Redwood AE): we compared to two baselines: your in-house CPU-based service (worse latency) and Velox. Redwood outperformed CPU baseline across the board and was competitive vs Velox.
09:30 Priya (Novena): the p95 for 512 tokens seemed high — can we do a hybrid: keep long-contexts on fp16 and short on q4 to balance?
09:45 Markus (Redwood SE): yes that's possible via routing policy; we can do request-based routing by prompt length. slight complexity in the stack but doable.
10:02 Aisha (Novena): any observed memory OOM at high concurrency?
10:09 Markus (Redwood SE): we had one OOM during the batch-16 512-token test, caused by an under-estimated dynamic memory overhead. fix is to adjust per-request memory accounting and reduce max-batch for large sequences.
10:32 Priya (Novena): okay, so immediate next steps technically are: re-run quant variations, run batch sweeps, and tweak kernel selector. operationally: send cost math, schedule security sync.
10:50 Sofia (Redwood AE): yes. i'll recap at the end.
11:03 (pause / cross-talk)
11:20 Markus (Redwood SE): quick note on the profiler artifacts — some symbols were obfuscated in our build, so the flamegraph may show "libcompute" rather than specific kernel names; i'm adding a symbol map to the artifact upload.
11:45 Kenji (Novena): thanks, that helps triage.
12:02 Priya (Novena): about Velox comparisons — their published numbers were done with a different transformer variant; how confident are we that we're comparing apples to apples?
12:18 Markus (Redwood SE): it's not exact — i annotated the spreadsheet with differences in sequence length distribution and batch policy. the replay we ran is the closest approximation but there will always be vendor and config delta.
12:40 Aisha (Novena): on quality — for the rare hallucinations with q4, could we run a heldout prompt set with scoring to estimate regression rate?
12:52 Markus (Redwood SE): yes, we can run scoring and surface the top n failure modes. i'll add that to the run plan.
13:10 Priya (Novena): timeline — can we get updated runs by next thursday (2025-11-13)?
13:17 Markus (Redwood SE): yes, i'll prioritize the quant+batch sweep and upload logs by then.
13:28 Sofia (Redwood AE): security sync week of 11/17, i'll propose times after this call.
13:37 (short silence)
13:45 Sofia (Redwood AE): quick commercial note — if you go dedicated we'll need a short addendum to your pilot contract for reserved burst capacity. nothing big but heads up.
14:02 Priya (Novena): understood. can you send the contract snippet?
14:07 Sofia (Redwood AE): yes, will include with the cost breakdown.
14:18 Kenji (Novena): any questions about monitoring — will the Redwood Console give us per-route latency and token cost?
14:28 Markus (Redwood SE): yes, there's token-level cost and per-model per-route metrics; we can add a dashboard for your endpoints.
14:40 Aisha (Novena): great.
15:00 Sofia (Redwood AE): OK recap — action items: markus to run quant and batch sweeps (due 11/13), sofia to send updated cost/latency spreadsheet and contract snippet (due 11/14), priya to confirm SLA and checklist (due 11/18). security sync proposed for week of 11/17. we'll also share profiler artifacts and a symbol map. any final Qs?
15:28 Priya (Novena): nope, thanks everyone. this was useful.
15:35 Sofia (Redwood AE): thanks, talk soon.
